source_text: Qui occultorum dispensationis mysteriorum omnem implevit providentiam ac dispositionem in caelo in sinu Patris, et in spelunca in ulnis matris, in praesepio requievit. Chori Angelici circumcingebant eum, in caelo gloriam concinentes, et in terra pacem adnuntiantes. In caelo a dextris Patris sedebat; et in praesepio, ut super Cherubim requiescebat. Thronus revera et hic erat Cherubicus; Thronus regalis; sanctus sanctorum; solus super terram gloriosus; sanctis sanctior; in quo requievit Christus Deus noster. Cui gloria, honor, et imperium, cum immaculatissimo Patre, et sanctissimo ac vivifico Spiritu: nunc et semper, et in saecula saeculorum, Amen.
thought_title: The manger as a royal and cherubic throne
orientation: The preacher is closing the homily at the birth in the cave and manger described just before.
pass_a_gloss: He who fulfilled all the forethought and ordering of the hidden mysteries of the dispensation, in heaven in the bosom of the Father, and in the cave in the arms of the mother, rested in the manger. Angelic choirs were encircling him, singing glory together in heaven, and announcing peace on earth. In heaven he was sitting at the right hands of the Father; and in the manger, as upon the Cherubim he was resting. In truth even this here was a Cherubic throne; a royal throne; a holy of holies; alone glorious over the earth; holier than holy things; in which rested Christ our God. To whom be glory and honor and rule, with the most stainless Father, and the most holy and life giving Spirit: now and always, and into ages of ages, Amen.

choices.why: Keeps mysterium as mystery per glossary and dispensatio as ordering, not adding secret.

pass_b_english: He who fulfilled all forethought and ordering of the hidden mysteries of the dispensation rested in a manger: in heaven in the bosom of the Father (John 1:18), and in a cave in the arms of his mother. Angelic choirs encircled him, singing glory in heaven and proclaiming peace on earth (Luke 2:14).

In heaven he sat at the right hand of the Father, and in the manger he rested as upon the Cherubim. For even this was truly a Cherubic throne, a royal throne, a holy of holies, alone glorious on earth and holier than the saints, in which Christ our God rested. To him be glory and honor and dominion, with the most spotless Father and the most holy and life giving Spirit, now and always and forever and ever, Amen.
